wheel.bolt_pattern: 6x139.7 (6x5.5") on half-ton K5s; 8-lug on one-ton axle swaps

max_tire.note: Hogback Fabrication on CK5: a stock K5 fits 32s without trimming and 33s with minor trimming. Other owners report 33s touching the inner fender at full lock and full bump. On 16-in wheels, 285/75R16 is reported not to rub. For 33x12.50s, one member suggests 15x8 wheels at about 3.5 in backspacing.
Offroad Design's 1988 Suburban (same chassis) ran 33x12.50R15s on 15x8 steel wheels with 3 in of lift at the front and 4 in at the rear, plus a dropped pitman arm and 4.5-in bump stops.
CK5 members: 33s clear without rubbing on a 4-in lift, while 35s rub and need some trimming. Plenty of owners run 35s on 4 in with modest trimming.

items.title: Rear brake drum balance weights can loosen aluminum wheels
items.summary: On 1982 Blazer, Jimmy and C10/C15 trucks with aluminum wheels, the drum balance weights could contact the wheel, loosen the lug nuts and break the studs (1,633 vehicles).

items.title: Composite front brake rotors can separate from corrosion
items.summary: Road-salt corrosion at the joint between the stamped steel center and cast outer section of the rotor could let them separate. The campaign covered Blazer, K10/K20, Suburban and GMC equivalents (341,364 vehicles).

timeline.change: 'Rounded Line' square body launches. The truck is 7 in longer overall on a 2.5-in longer wheelbase. The body is fully open behind the windshield, with a removable hardtop or convertible top. NP205 part-time or NP203 full-time 4WD; Dana 44 front, 12-bolt rear. Tilt wheel optional
400 V8 joins the K-series engine list. Chevrolet adds the Scottsdale and Silverado trims, and Silverado becomes the top trim. Catalytic converters on trucks under 6,000 lb GVWR
Half-cab body with a fixed steel roof over the front seats and a removable rear top, through 1991. Blazer Chalet / Jimmy Casa Grande camper (1976–77, about 1,800 built)
GM corporate 10-bolt front axle phased in alongside the Dana 44. Power windows and locks offered for the first time
Full-time 4WD (NP203) dropped from K-series. NP205s get a slip-yoke rear output
Facelift with available stacked square headlamps and reduced weight. NP208 shift-on-the-fly transfer case and automatic locking hubs
6.2 L diesel V8 (130 hp / 240 lb-ft at launch). 700R4 four-speed overdrive automatic available
S-10 Blazer arrives, so the big truck becomes the 'Full-Size Blazer' and the 'K-Jimmy'. M1009 CUCV production begins (1983–87). The 250 six, standard through 1982, is no longer the base engine
Throttle-body injection on all gas engines. The trucks become the R/V series (V10 Blazer, V-Jimmy) as GMT400 pickups take the C/K name. From here on the 350 is the standard engine
K5 emblems dropped; fender-mounted mast antenna replaces the windshield antenna; trip odometer
GMT400-style grille; NP241 transfer case; 30-spline 10-bolt axle shafts; serpentine belt on the 5.7. Cheyenne returns as the base Chevrolet trim
Rear-wheel anti-lock brakes, electronic speedometer, double-sided galvanized exterior panels, rear three-point belts
Final year. 700R4 renamed 4L60; CS130 alternator. Replaced for 1992 by the GMT400 Blazer and GMC Yukon

identify.intro: After 35 to 50 years, many K5s have had engine, axle and transfer case swaps, and plenty of GMC Jimmys have been re-badged. These checks help you work out what a truck started out as.

items.head: Front axle
items.body: Torque King says the GM 10-bolt front cover is an oval about 11 in high by 10-1/4 in wide with no flat sides, unlike the Dana 44 cover. GMSquareBody members also note the two small ears on the 10-bolt housing. Dana 44s are typical of 1973–76, either could be fitted in 1977–78, and the 10-bolt is typical from 1979. Dana 44 and 10-bolt shafts don't interchange.

items.head: Transfer case
items.body: NP205: a one-piece cast-iron case with a small three-bolt idler cover on the back and an ID tag above the front output. NP203: about 22–23 in long, in four bolted sections with a range box on the front and its tag on the chain case. NP208 (1981–88) and NP241 (1989–91) are aluminum, chain-driven cases, and the NP241's tag is on the rear of the case.

items.head: 305 or 350?
items.body: CK5 members warn that 305s get sold as 350s. Wikipedia notes that 1981-on 305s used smaller 56 cc combustion chambers, against 76 cc. Check the casting numbers and the engine code before you pay a 350 price.

items.head: Year by the front end
items.body: 1973–80 trucks mostly have round headlamps (Silverado-trim C/K trucks got square ones for 1980). From 1981 there's a new front end with available stacked square headlamps. The 1988 trucks lose the K5 badge and get a fender-mounted antenna. The 1989–91 trucks have the flatter, GMT400-style grille.

items.head: A real M1009
items.body: Genuine M1009s have the 6.2 diesel, a TH400 and an NP208, 10-bolt axles with 3.08 gears and an Eaton automatic rear locker, 10.00-15 tires, and a 24/12-volt system with two batteries, two alternators, a firewall glow-plug resistor pack and a NATO slave receptacle in the grille. Blackout lights, a brush guard and a rifle rack were standard.

items.head: Model naming
items.body: Chevrolet badges read K5 until 1988. GM officially called it the Full-Size Blazer from 1983 and the V10 / V1500 Blazer from 1987. GMC's twin was the Jimmy, then the K-Jimmy, then from 1987 the V-Jimmy.

capability.note: Army towed-load rating; Wikipedia says six-cylinder Blazers weren't recommended for towing

capability.v: 9.6 mpg at 45 mph (350 V8) · 13.7 mpg at 45 mph (250 I6)

values.intro: Prices depend more on the build than the year. Clean stock trucks bring steady money, M1009s are the cheap way into a diesel K5, and LS-swapped restomods take the top results.
values.note: Based on the 15 most recent Bring a Trailer sales of 1973–91 K5 Blazers (August–October 2026): $4,600 to $130,000, median $29,500. Stock trucks mostly sold for $15,000–38,500, a 1991 Silverado brought $80,000, a 1984 M1009 sold for $20,500, and an LSA-powered 1973 set the top at $130,000. Nine more trucks were bid to between $8,800 and $68,000 without selling.
